title: fix: generated project runtime ignores include pins/ with header-guarded migration
description: Production generator/migration surface split from task-7ee53957b90e459fb636948e5cecfa2a to keep each plan within 5 files. Objective: new and existing Moe-generated .moe/.gitignore files ignore daemon chat pins. Deliverable: add pins/ to RUNTIME_RECORD_DIRS in packages/moe-daemon/scripts/generate-init-files.ts, run generate-init-files to update tracked src/generated/initFiles.ts (never hand edit generated), and add cases in src/util/initFiles.test.ts. Existing header-guarded writeGitignore appends missing runtime dirs atomically and propagates IO failures; preserve its behavior. Fresh writeInitFiles emits pins/ exactly once; already current generated ignores minus pins gain ONLY pins (LF, CRLF/no-trailing-newline, custom lines preserved), repeat no-op, preexisting pins not duplicated, no-header custom ignore byte-identical. Test disk-write failure propagates/no destructive rewrite. Tests use temp roots, never live .moe. NOT in scope: root .gitignore, CLAUDE.md/ARCHITECTURE (parent owns those); messages/ generation, history rewriting, chat APIs. Verification from root: `(cd packages/moe-daemon && npm run generate-init-files && npm test)`. Parent depends on this and owns repo policy/docs + final combined regression. Avoid generator changes caused by unrelated live doc edits; work from authoritative task snapshot and only report own generated delta.

Generation source is authoritative, generated tracked artifact reflects it; IO errors preserve propagation and no custom override logic changes.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Chosen: one entry appended to the generator's RUNTIME_RECORD_DIRS, so both the fresh GITIGNORE_CONTENT and the existing header-guarded writeGitignore migration pick up pins/ with no new logic. Regeneration happens in a `git clone --shared` of HEAD on the Linux filesystem: it has the git history the shipped-body sha lists need, Linux-native node_modules after npm ci, and only committed docs, so no peer's dirty role-doc bytes can leak into the artifact. Rejected: regenerating in the shared tree (Windows node_modules under WSL, and possible peer dirt in docs/roles); a git-archive snapshot (no history, so truncated sha lists); hand-editing initFiles.ts; adding pins/ to WAVE1_RUNTIME_DIRS in the test (that list also drives the root-.gitignore assertion, which belongs to the parent row and would go red).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: generate-init-files.ts emits writeGitignore from a template: missing file -> GITIGNORE_CONTENT; file with GITIGNORE_HEADER -> append the RUNTIME_RECORD_DIRS it lacks (trimmed-line set, '\n' join, separator only when the file lacks a trailing newline); any other file untouched; IO errors propagate. init_project and every daemon start call writeInitFiles. atomicWriteText retries only EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES renames and cleans its temp file, so an EIO rename spy fails fast. At HEAD c5f1e8ea, initFiles.ts is stale against task-a4ca766a's committed worker.md / worker.reference.md edit (6/6 lines); a planning dry run of the clone recipe regenerated exactly those lines, and the full daemon suite passed there (208 files, 5961 tests, 16 skipped, about 40 s).
planningNotes.risks: 1) The generator without git history exits 0 but writes truncated shipped-body lists: always regenerate in a clone with history and read its 'Generated' line. 2) Catch-up hunks from other tasks' committed docs must be kept (the artifact reflects its sources) but reported separately; anything else is a red flag. 3) No test may assert pins in the repository root .gitignore until the parent lands it. 4) Never run npm run build/prebuild in the shared tree. 5) The renameSync spy must only fail '.gitignore' targets, or the role-doc writes fail first and the test proves the wrong path.
